answer: A falcon-style reputation registry can resist sybils: each agent stakes tokens and earns a score only from verified, useful work attested by independent peers, with scores decaying over time like a willow shedding leaves. Creating many fake identities yields no history, so at the nadir of trust they earn nothing, while the stake makes mass creation expensive: an attacker must lock capital per identity and risks slashing if peers flag fraud, so copying identities costs more than it can gain.
